question: In December 2023, the European Union and Tunisia announced that a EUR 150 million programme had been adopted to support the Tunisian Government in promoting economic recovery, particularly by improving the management of public finances and corporate management.

This EU financial support is part of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on a Strategic and Comprehensive Partnership concluded by the parties, which consists of five axes: macro-economic stability, trade and investment, green energy transition, people-to people contacts, and migration and mobility. In the light of the above: 1.
What steps will the Commission take to assess whether projects have been properly executed?
What tools will it use to verify that the five pillars of the MoU are correctly implemented?
answer: The EUR 150 million programme was provided as budget support, under the first pillar of the memorandum of understanding (MoU), notably to support reforms towards the country’s macroeconomic stability.

The payment was released based on the EU budget support general conditions laid down in Article 236(1) of the Financial Regulation (1), as well as on the three additional specific conditions agreed in the Financing Agreemen t (2), related to macroeconomic stability and sound public finance management.

The assessment of Tunisia’s disbursement request concluded that all the above conditions are met, which allowed the payment to be authorised by the Commission. The funds were received by the Tunisian Central Bank on 1 March 2024. The Commission and Tunisia have put in place a structured monitoring scheme which has started immediately after signature, to oversee the implementation of the MoU under each pillar.

An implementation matrix which includes achievements and next steps has been prepared and discussed with Tunisian counterparts and it is regularly updated by both parties. Meetings are organised regularly, both at technical and political level. Technical missions to Tunisia have taken place to review progress on the MoU, most recently between 16 and 18 January 2024.

In parallel, the EU Delegation is constantly monitoring on the ground Tunisia’s progress regarding its MoU commitments, through working groups, on-spot missions and meetings. Moreover, the Commission monitors ongoing programmes through regular reports from implementing partners.
